clue.text: Hoskins takes ecstasy in extra small undies

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so the pair on either side of 'takes' go inside what follows 'in'

parts.note: a frill is an unnecessary extra
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the setter, Hoskins, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to taking a pill and squeezing into very skimpy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra small' reads as one size, but it splits into an extra (a frill) and S for small, with the setter and the drug placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is an informal word for women's lacy underwear, a kind of undies.

clue.text: Able to pocket second bunch of fives

indicators.note: pocketing something means putting it away inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: fit means able or in condition to do something
S is the standard abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone capable of snooker-style potting slips a second ball away.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunch of fives is old British slang for a clenched hand used for punching, the five being the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase pictures five fingers bundled together, which is exactly a closed hand ready to punch.

clue.text: Premium ale rise going to be around a pound?

indicators.note: being around something means surrounding it, so the other words enclose the little word next to them
the words are going, falling apart, so their letters are free to take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Good beer is about to cost nearly a pound more, a pub-goer grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound looks like money in a beer-price story, but it is the weight, and the question mark warns that it is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The pound weight belongs to the old British system of units, so it is one example of an imperial measure.

clue.text: Relaxed cooking the last of Chinese noodles

indicators.note: cooking turns raw ingredients into something new, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only, so just one letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of Chinese

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds by making the last of the Chinese noodles.
explanation.definitionFit: To relax a grip or a knot is to slacken it, so relaxed and loosened are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Consumer society rejected by holy festival

indicators.note: something rejected is turned away and left out, so a letter is dropped from the festival

parts.note: Easter is the Christian festival of the resurrection
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Consumerism is condemned by the church at a religious holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer society' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who consumes food is an eater, so the two nouns name the same person.

clue.text: A place to race an F1 Ferrari?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a racecourse in North Yorkshire
second meaning: Ferrari's Formula One cars are famously painted red

explanation.walkthrough: Redcar is a seaside town in North Yorkshire with a horse-racing course; split in two, the name describes a scarlet racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: The town hosts horse races, and a Formula One Ferrari is famously a scarlet motor vehicle.

clue.text: Outdo formerly ranked player, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the phrase and listen to it rather than read its spelling

parts.note: a player who used to be seeded in a tournament is an ex-seed

explanation.surface: A tennis player who has lost their ranking still hopes to beat the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Seeded players are those ranked to avoid each other in early rounds of a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to go beyond them, which is what exceed means as a verb.

clue.text: Die — result of till explosion in Harry Ramsden's?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an idiom for passing away

definitions.text: result of till explosion in Harry Ramsden's
definitions.meaning: second meaning: money from a burst register landing in your fried potatoes

explanation.walkthrough: Harry Ramsden's is a British fish-and-chip restaurant chain, so a till exploding there would scatter money into the food. The idiom comes from gamblers exchanging their chips for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom originates with gamblers leaving the table and swapping their tokens for money, a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: New royal sent up in a resounding manner

indicators.note: up here means in turmoil or amiss, as in 'what's up', so the letters are disordered

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly crowned royal is dispatched with a great fanfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' looks like a single phrase meaning mocked; only 'up' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something resonant echoes and booms, so the adverb describes acting in a resounding, ringing way.

clue.text: Brochure about river and very small stream

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps round the river letter

parts.note: a brochure is a small promotional booklet
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A tourist leaflet describes a river and a tiny stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook is a stream and the -let ending makes it diminutive, so a tiny stream.

clue.text: Second drink left by Phil's missus

parts.note: to sup is to drink
port is the left side of a ship
Prince Philip's wife was Elizabeth Regina, ER

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their drink while sitting with a man called Phil's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil is Prince Philip, whose wife was the Queen, ER. 'Second' looks like an ordinal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A second in a duel or boxing match is the backer who assists a fighter, so a supporter.

clue.text: Hipsters hanging around square models

indicators.note: to hang around something is to surround it, so the first word goes outside the next

parts.note: cats is old jazz slang for hip people
S is short for square

explanation.surface: Trendy young people loiter around a town square full of fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Casts are moulded replicas of a shape, and models are likewise copies of an object.

clue.text: Prepare to polish off fine cheese

indicators.note: polishing something off finishes it and takes it away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to brief someone is to prepare them with information
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: Get ready to wolf down a lovely bit of cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine cheese' reads as a quality description; fine is a separate letter to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese named after the region of France it comes from.

clue.text: Old African in a shed or building

indicators.note: building means constructing something from parts, so the letters are put together afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly man from Africa sits in a garden shed or some other building.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe, so a person from there is an African of an old country.

clue.text: Tree decoration, not very heavy, just one left

indicators.note: where there were two of the letter for left, keeping just one means the other goes

parts.note: fairly light means quite but not very heavy

explanation.surface: A Christmas tree ornament is quite light, with only one left in the box.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for 'not very heavy' has two Ls, L standing for left; drop one to leave just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy lights are strings of tiny bulbs hung on a Christmas tree as an ornament.

clue.text: Fab to floor former Shadow Chancellor?

parts.note: to floor someone is to astonish them
Ed Balls was the Labour Shadow Chancellor until 2015

explanation.surface: A fabulous result: to knock down the former opposition finance spokesman.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was the opposition's finance spokesman in Britain and later a 'Strictly Come Dancing' contestant.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazeballs is jokey slang for brilliant or wonderful, the same enthusiastic praise as fab.

clue.text: US toilet sat on by dodgy aimer

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written
can is US slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A US toilet is used by someone with poor aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US toilet' looks like one thing; US alone is the definition. In a down answer the jumbled letters sit on top of the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: US used as an adjective, as in US citizens, means belonging to the United States, which is what American means.

clue.text: Month or day with an O in it?

indicators.note: having a letter in it means that letter is placed inside, splitting the day

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday
the letter as printed

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which month or weekday contains the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A moon in poetry is a lunar month, the time between one new moon and the next.

clue.text: Runner crop in small English nursery?

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the abbreviations that follow it

parts.note: a ski is a runner that slides on snow
S is the abbreviation for small
to crop is to cut off or lop
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A gardener trims a plant growing in a small English plant nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: A nursery slope is the gentle beginners' run at a skiing resort; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginners learn on a gentle run called the nursery slope, one kind of piste for skiing.

clue.text: Last love's lost by lover boy in this city

indicators.note: what is lost is no longer there, so a letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: Romeo is Shakespeare's archetypal young lover

indicators.note: last points to the final letter only of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of love

explanation.surface: A romantic young man loses his final sweetheart while in an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'love' is also O, the shape of zero, and it is the final O of the lover's name that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is the capital city of Italy, setting the scene of this little story.

clue.text: One ringing to inform of a loss?

definitions.text: One ringing to inform of a loss

parts.words: One ringing to inform of a loss
parts.note: surface reading: a person making a phone call to break bad news; setter's reading: the tolling of a church bell to announce a funeral

explanation.walkthrough: The ringing sounds like a telephone call, but it is a bell sounded slowly to mark someone's passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A single bell tolled after a death announces a parish loss, and figuratively signals the end of anything.

clue.text: Rich kind of sauce date put on earl's bottom

parts.note: mint sauce is served with lamb
E is an abbreviation for earl
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A wealthy aristocrat sits on a rich sauce and a date.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the date letter sits under the earl, at its bottom. Minted is British slang for very wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Minted is British slang for very wealthy, as if one had coined one's own money.

clue.text: Large institute with faculty debt

parts.note: L is the size abbreviation for large
I is the abbreviation for institute
a faculty is a natural ability

explanation.surface: A big college with its teaching staff is running into the red.
explanation.walkthrough: Faculty suggests a university department in the surface, but here it is a mental power.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting a liability is an amount owed, which is exactly what a debt is.

clue.text: Long story describing the end of empire

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so the story encloses the letter

parts.note: a yarn is a long tale

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of empire

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale tells of an empire's fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long story' looks like one phrase; long is a verb here, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to want it badly, the same verb sense as yearn.

clue.text: Temperature put out by chimney fire

indicators.note: something put out is ejected, so a letter is thrown out of the next word

parts.note: a chimney stack is the part above a roof
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: Heat escapes from a chimney when a fire is burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chimney fire' reads as a blaze; fire is the verb meaning dismiss from a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack an employee is to dismiss them from their job, which is the informal verb fire.

clue.text: Tantrist regularly in flagrante delicto

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A practitioner of tantric sex is often caught in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: A tantrist follows Tantra, whose sexual practices give the surface its joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means caught in the very act, and the idiom at it means busy having sex.

clue.text: Wasted occupants of sauna tucking into G&T

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so these letters go within the drink

parts.note: the gin-and-tonic letters, split apart

indicators.note: the occupants of a word are the letters living inside it, its middle

parts.note: the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Drunk sauna-goers are knocking back gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunk in the surface; here it means emaciated. G&T is gin and tonic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wasted by illness is thin and bony, which is what gaunt describes.

clue.text: One cutting a mutated man to section bone-type?

definitions.text: One cutting a mutated man to section bone-type

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the single letter is inserted

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: mutated means changed in form, so the letters of the following words change order

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
S is an abbreviation for section
a T-bone is a type of bone in a steak

explanation.surface: A dissector cuts up a deformed man's body, studying bone types.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also building it: the numeral one cuts between the jumbled man and the closing letters for section and T-bone.
explanation.definitionFit: An anatomist dissects bodies to study their structure, which is cutting a man into sections.

clue.text: Butt-clenching attempt to get 'with it'

indicators.note: clenching grips something tightly inside, so the attempt encloses the butt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a butt is the end of something, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: A comic picture of a buttock-tightening workout done to look fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: 'With it' is dated slang for fashionable and up to date, the same as trendy.

clue.text: Posh nerd excited by regular vest and pants?

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled about

parts.note: taken as written
set means fixed or regular, as in a set routine

explanation.surface: An upper-class geek gets worked up over an ordinary vest and pants.
explanation.walkthrough: Underset normally means an undercurrent in the sea; the question mark lets vest and pants be a playful 'underwear set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully, a matching vest and pants form an underwear set, punning on the real word for a subsurface current.
